Free Options [...] So we built the tool we needed as operators:

🔍 Visibility: we ask your buyers' real questions on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews every day, and track who gets named

❓ Why you lost: every lost question, who won it, and what the answer leaned on

📚 Citations: the reviews, roundups and comparisons AI actually trusts

🛠️ Fixes + agents: drafts built from the pages already winning. You approve, agents publish, verify the answers changed, and learn from every change

One operator principle we built in: AI answers are noisy (up to 27% of names change day to day), so every number carries a confidence interval. If a change is just noise, we'll tell you, not take credit for it.

In private beta, 5 teams are already paying us. Today we're opening it up. [...] Quick context on me: I'm an engineer turned growth operator and a second-time founder. My first startup was Scholarnex, an edtech I co-founded straight out of engineering school. Since then I've spent a decade running growth hands-on at ByteDance, Foundit, Mahindra Finance and IDFC FIRST Bank, helping move $600M+ in revenue. I'm building Proofsource with Amit, who ran growth at Uber and slice.

Then the channel changed under us. Organic traffic went flat, but "ChatGPT" kept showing up in our "how did you hear about us?" field. Real sign-ups, from a channel we couldn't see. We had no idea what ChatGPT was saying about us, which questions it recommended us for, or who it named instead. Every tool in our stack was built for ten blue links. AI names five or six companies and stops.
